about: Spoken explanations with deliberate errors and omissions, for teach it back. Each lists what was said (parts, stated relations), the wrong claims as stated and as corrected, words for parts that were NOT said (none of them may appear in the student's purple drawing), and the gaps a good check finds. Keywords match a word's start, so 'serv' matches 'server' and 'servers'.

fixtures.name: consistent-hashing
fixtures.explanation: Okay so consistent hashing. Um, you have a circle, like a ring of numbers, and each server gets a spot on the circle by hashing its name. Then when a key comes in you hash the key too and it lands somewhere on the circle, and then the key goes to the previous server, like the one just before it going backwards. And there's also replication, I think.

wrong_claims.claim: the key goes to the previous server

expected_gaps.gap: the key goes to the next server clockwise
adding or removing a server moves only a few keys

fixtures.name: tcp-handshake
fixtures.explanation: So the TCP handshake. The client sends a SYN to the server, then the server sends back an ACK, and then the connection is open and they can send data. Um, and the sequence numbers are random.

wrong_claims.claim: the server answers with a plain ACK

expected_gaps.gap: the server answers SYN-ACK, not ACK
the client sends a final ACK as the third step

fixtures.name: binary-search
fixtures.explanation: Binary search. You take a list and you look at the middle element, and if the thing you want is bigger you go left, and if it's smaller you go right, and you keep halving it until you find it. It's O of n.

expected_gaps.gap: a bigger target is searched on the right
it is O of log n
the list must be sorted

fixtures.name: lru-cache
fixtures.explanation: A cache is a small fast memory that sits in front of the database. When you read something you check the cache first, and if it's there that's a hit and you return it. If it's not there you go to the database. And when the cache is full you kick out the oldest item, the one that was put in first.

wrong_claims.claim: evicts the item put in first

expected_gaps.gap: evict the least recently used, not the first put in
on a miss the value is put in the cache

fixtures.name: photosynthesis
fixtures.explanation: Photosynthesis is how plants make food. The leaves take in oxygen from the air and water from the roots, and with sunlight in the chloroplasts they make glucose, and they give off carbon dioxide.

expected_gaps.gap: they take in carbon dioxide, not oxygen
they give off oxygen, not carbon dioxide

fixtures.name: dns-resolution
fixtures.explanation: When you type a website, the browser asks the DNS resolver for the IP address. The resolver asks the root server, and the root server gives back the IP address of the website, and then the browser connects to it. Oh and the answer gets cached.

wrong_claims.claim: the root server gives the IP address

expected_gaps.gap: the root only points to the TLD server
the authoritative server gives the actual address

fixtures.name: merge-sort
fixtures.explanation: Merge sort. You split the array in half, and you keep splitting until each piece has one element. Then you merge the pieces back together. And it sorts in place so it doesn't need any extra memory.

wrong_claims.claim: it sorts in place with no extra memory

expected_gaps.gap: merging compares the fronts so the result is sorted
it needs extra memory, not in place

fixtures.name: supply-and-demand
fixtures.explanation: So when the price goes up, people want to buy more of it, that's demand. And sellers want to sell more when the price goes up, that's supply. And where they cross is the equilibrium price.

expected_gaps.gap: people buy less when the price rises

fixtures.name: mark-and-sweep
fixtures.explanation: The garbage collector starts from the roots, like global variables and the stack, and it marks every object it can reach. Then it goes through memory and frees everything that is marked.

expected_gaps.gap: it frees what is NOT marked

fixtures.name: vaccines
fixtures.explanation: A vaccine puts a weakened or dead virus into your body, and your red blood cells make antibodies against it, and then the next time you see the real virus you already have the antibodies.

expected_gaps.gap: white blood cells (B cells) make antibodies
memory cells are what last and respond fast

fixtures.name: two-phase-commit
fixtures.explanation: Two phase commit is for distributed transactions. The coordinator sends a prepare message to all the participants, and each one votes yes or no. Then if most of them vote yes, the coordinator tells everyone to commit.

expected_gaps.gap: commit only if every participant votes yes
if any votes no, everyone aborts

fixtures.name: newtons-second-law
fixtures.explanation: Newton's second law says force equals mass times velocity. So if you push something heavier with the same force, it moves slower.

expected_gaps.gap: force equals mass times acceleration

fixtures.name: hash-table
fixtures.explanation: A hash table stores key value pairs. You run the key through a hash function to get an index into an array, and you put the value in that bucket. If two keys land in the same bucket that's a collision, and you can keep a little linked list in the bucket for them. So lookups are usually constant time.

fixtures.name: osmosis
fixtures.explanation: Osmosis is when water moves across a membrane from where there's less water to where there's more water. It keeps going until both sides are the same.

wrong_claims.claim: water moves from less water to more water

expected_gaps.gap: water moves from more water to less water (toward more solute)
the membrane is semi-permeable: water passes, solutes do not

retries.explanation: Okay let me try the comparison part again. If the thing you want is bigger than the middle you go right, and if it's smaller you go left.
The server actually sends back a SYN-ACK, and then the client sends a final ACK, and then the connection is open.
